subject: SLA baseline discussion: uptime commitment and monthly credits (TideCore)
messages:
From: Emily Ramos <emily.ramos@tidecore.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: TideCore Legal <legal@tidecore.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA baseline for TideCore - uptime & monthly credits

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — TideCore is excited about Redwood's latency profile for batched inference. Before we move to procurement, our legal and ops teams asked for a quick alignment on two items in your standard SLA template:

1) Baseline uptime percentage: our procurement team wants 99.95% as a target for production endpoints. We saw 99.9% in the draft — can you confirm whether 99.95% is achievable on Dedicated capacity or what the carveouts are?

2) Monthly credit mechanics: TideCore prefers a capped monthly service credit (as a percentage of invoice) rather than per-incident pro-rata credits. Can you share an example cap structure and whether Redwood will allow a fixed-dollar cap for the first 12 months?

We'd like to have a short call next week with Ben from Sales and your legal contact to close these points. I attached a brief RFC that captures TideCore's ask and the use-case (sensitive production inference with strict latency SLAs).

Best,
Emily Ramos
Head of Platform Ops, TideCore
(em: emily.ramos@tidecore.com)

Attachments: TideCore_SLA_RFC_20261022.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA baseline for TideCore - uptime & monthly credits

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear note and the RFC. Looping in Ben (sales lead) and Kimberly (legal) so we can align internally and give you a concrete proposal. High-level responses below; will follow up with a short redline and a call invite.

Quick answers:
- Baseline uptime: Hosted standard is 99.9% by default. For Dedicated capacity we can negotiate to 99.95% provided there is a 12-month committed capacity profile and agreed maintenance windows. This typically requires a small uplift in the monthly commitment (we can quantify).
- Monthly credit mechanics: We prefer a percentage-of-monthly-invoice approach with a monthly cap expressed as a percentage (e.g., up to 50% of monthly charges) rather than fixed-dollar caps. That said, for enterprise deals we can accept a fixed-dollar cap tied to the committed spend in year one.

Action items I propose:
1) Ben to propose two alternative commitment bands (Committed-GPU hours + estimated tokens) that map to 99.95% availability and the corresponding uplift.
2) Kimberly to propose a credit cap option (percent or fixed-dollar) and the maintenance carveouts that preserve the higher uptime target.
3) Quick call — 30 minutes to agree on the band and draft a short amendment to the standard SLA template.

Can you do Tuesday or Wednesday next week (Oct 27–28)?

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0113

Attachment referenced: SLA_Template_v3.docx (see link)

Subject: Re: SLA baseline for TideCore - uptime & monthly credits

Emily — appreciate the RFC and the clarity. I ran a quick capacity sketch with Infra and we can support a contractual 99.95% uptime for Dedicated pools under the following conditions:

- Commitment: 12-month minimum reserved GPU pool (we'll define the size in committed compute-hours).
- Maintenance windows: one weekly 4-hour window (customer opinionated scheduling possible with 30-day notice) and up to 12 planned maintenance days per year that are carveouts to uptime measurement.
- Escalation support: 24x7 P1 on-call and a dedicated technical account manager included in the uplift for the higher SLA.

Credit structure options (examples):
A) Percentage cap: remedial credits up to 50% of monthly invoice for total monthly downtime beyond thresholds. Credits issued as percent-of-monthly-invoice and applied to the next invoice.
B) Fixed-dollar cap (first 12 months): cap equal to 30% of the committed monthly spend in month 1 (one-time fixed-dollar cap) with an option to renegotiate after month 12.

We prefer A for predictability, but B is achievable for enterprise with procurement sign-off. Kimberly — any immediate legal notes to flag?

Next step: Logan, can you propose two commitment bands and we’ll map cost uplift to each? Emily, if you can confirm expected baseline compute and token volumes we’ll size bands and share a short amendment draft before the call.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLA baseline for TideCore - uptime & monthly credits

Hi Emily — following our internal review and Ben's capacity sketch, attached is a short amendment draft that captures: 99.95% uptime for Dedicated pools, the maintenance carveouts, and both credit options (percentage cap and fixed-dollar cap for year one).

Key legal points that TideCore should note:
- Measurement window: uptime measured monthly, calculated as (total minutes in month - service downtime minutes) / total minutes. Planned maintenance and force majeure are excluded as defined.
- Credits: credits are applied as account-level invoice adjustments and do not constitute refunds; they also do not affect termination rights.
- Liability: credits remain the sole and exclusive remedy for service availability in the amendment. We can discuss exceptions for systemic failures during the negotiation call.

Emily — I've scheduled a 30-minute sync for Oct 29 at 10:00 AM PT to walk through the amendment and finalize the band. If TideCore prefers a fixed-dollar cap for procurement simplicity, we can include the option and a one-year review clause.

Please find the draft amendment here: https://redwood.teamdrive.com/sla-templates/SLA_Template_v3.docx

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
